The children have worked extremely
hard preparing their

,

confidence, creativity and enthusiasm
they have shown. Standing up in
front of others and sharing your ideas
takes a great deal of courage, and we
would like to say a

huge well done to
every pupil who has put themselves
forward and taken part so
passionately.
Voting has been underway in the

today, giving pupils the
opportunity to have their say and
choose the children they feel will best
represent them. It has been
wonderful to see our pupils engaging
so enthusiastically with the process
and understanding the importance of
having a voice within their school
community.

We are very proud of everyone who
has taken part, and whatever the
final result, each and every candidate
should feel incredibly proud of what
they have achieved. We are now
eagerly awaiting the results and

look
forward to introducing our new House
Captains, School Councillors, Eco
Warriors and Happiness Heroes next
week!

💛 Could you help keep our PTFA
going?

Our PTFA is a wonderful part of the
Warboys Primary Academy
community, helping to bring exciting
events and opportunities to our
children while raising much-needed
funds for the school.However,

we
urgently need more parents and carers
to get involved.

Following several of our valued
committee members stepping down
as their children finished at the
school last year, we are now facing a
very real challenge.

We are losing our
Treasurer, along with other
experienced members, and without
enough people willing to step forward,
we may have no choice but to fold the
PTFA.

We really don't want that to happen.
You might think you need lots of free
time or previous experience to join
the PTFA,

We need people
who can help in whatever way they
can. That could mean helping at an
event, coming along with ideas,
taking on a committee role, helping
with fundraising, or simply lending a
hand occasionally.

Every person who gets involved
makes the workload lighter for
everyone else — and helps us
continue providing those extra
experiences and opportunities
for our children.

Please come along, even if you're
unsure how you could help. Come and
meet the current PTFA, find out what
we do and see how you might be able
to get involved.

We genuinely need
your support. Without new volunteers,
the PTFA may not be able to continue.

Let's make sure we can keep doing
something really special for the
children of Warboys Primary
Academy.

A quick reminder that our PTFA sell
high‑quality

through their Facebook page. It’s a
great way to save money, support the
school, and give uniform items a new
life.Please check out their page if you
need any extra bits for the term

If you require any further
information or have any questions or
concerns, please don’t hesitate to get
in touch with us in the school office -
we’re here to help.

Want to learn more? Take a look
around our website at

— you’ll find
plenty of helpful information.

REMEMBER - If you feel that a child
is unsafe, then please use the
following ways to contact help.

Call Social Services on 0345 045 5203
and make a referral. This can be an
anonymous referral if this feels safer.

Call 999 IF CHILD IS IN
IMMEDIATE DANGER.

You can also use our emergency email
address
(safeguarding@wpa.education). BUT
please use the other options first, so
as not to delay help for a child.

look forward to seeing you there!

Booking Reminder

A reminder to parents and carers
wishing to book their child into the

wraparound provision provided by
YDP

that all bookings must be made
directly through the YDP booking
platform, which can be found

HERE

.
Please note that

YDP is a separate
provider

, and therefore the school
office is

unable to make or manage
bookings on behalf of families

.

Places are limited, so we strongly
encourage families to book as far in
advance as possible to avoid
disappointment.

If you need to make

If you have any questions, please

office directly

announcements.title: Attendance Update: Termly Pizza Parties (TAPP) & Appointment Guidelines
announcements.content:
Attendance Update for
September

As we begin the new academic year,
we are introducing a few updates to
our attendance procedures to support
pupils' success and celebrate excellent
attendance.

Medical appointments

will continue
to be authorised only when
appointment confirmation is provided
to the school office.

Optician
appointments

will no longer be
authorised from September, as these
can usually be arranged outside
school hours.

We are also delighted to launch our

Termly Attendance Pizza Parties
(TAPP).

Pupils achieving

98%
attendance or above

each term will be
invited to a special pizza party during
the final week of term and will
receive a raffle ticket for the chance
to win a

£50 Amazon voucher.

At Warboys Primary Academy, we
know that good attendance plays a
vital role in children's academic
achievement, social development and
wellbeing. Thank you for your
continued support in helping your
child attend school regularly and
arrive on time, giving them the very
best opportunity to thrive.

Term-time leave

We appreciate that unexpected events
can happen, and we’re always here to
support families where possible.

However, Cambridgeshire County
Council and the Department for
Education require schools to
authorise leave

only in exceptional
circumstances

—meaning rare,
unavoidable events.

Routine family holidays or planned
trips unfortunately do not meet this
threshold. You can find further
information here:

Non-attendance at school and the
law | Cambridgeshire County
Council

Thank you for your understanding
and cooperation.

💛 Could you help keep our PTFA
going?

Our PTFA is a wonderful part of the
Warboys Primary Academy
community, helping to bring exciting
events and opportunities to our
children while raising much-needed
funds for the school.However,

we
urgently need more parents and carers
to get involved.

Following several of our valued
committee members stepping down
as their children finished at the
school last year, we are now facing a
very real challenge.

We are losing our
Treasurer, along with other
experienced members, and without
enough people willing to step forward,
we may have no choice but to fold the
PTFA.

We really don't want that to happen.
You might think you need lots of free
time or previous experience to join
the PTFA,

We need people
who can help in whatever way they
can. That could mean helping at an
event, coming along with ideas,
taking on a committee role, helping
with fundraising, or simply lending a
hand occasionally.

Every person who gets involved
makes the workload lighter for
everyone else — and helps us
continue providing those extra
experiences and opportunities
for our children.

Please come along, even if you're
unsure how you could help. Come and
meet the current PTFA, find out what
we do and see how you might be able
to get involved.

We genuinely need
your support. Without new volunteers,
the PTFA may not be able to continue.

Let's make sure we can keep doing
something really special for the
children of Warboys Primary
Academy.

A quick reminder that our PTFA sell
high‑quality

through their Facebook page. It’s a
great way to save money, support the
school, and give uniform items a new
life.Please check out their page if you
need any extra bits for the term

If you require any further
information or have any questions or
concerns, please don’t hesitate to get
in touch with us in the school office -
we’re here to help.

Want to learn more? Take a look
around our website at

— you’ll find
plenty of helpful information.

REMEMBER - If you feel that a child
is unsafe, then please use the
following ways to contact help.

Call Social Services on 0345 045 5203
and make a referral. This can be an
anonymous referral if this feels safer.

Call 999 IF CHILD IS IN
IMMEDIATE DANGER.

You can also use our emergency email
address
(safeguarding@wpa.education). BUT
please use the other options first, so
as not to delay help for a child.

announcements.title: Attendance Update: Termly Pizza Parties (TAPP) & Appointment Guidelines
announcements.content:
Attendance Update for
September

As we begin the new academic year,
we are introducing a few updates to
our attendance procedures to support
pupils' success and celebrate excellent
attendance.

Medical appointments

will continue
to be authorised only when
appointment confirmation is provided
to the school office.

Optician
appointments

will no longer be
authorised from September, as these
can usually be arranged outside
school hours.

We are also delighted to launch our

Termly Attendance Pizza Parties
(TAPP).

Pupils achieving

98%
attendance or above

each term will be
invited to a special pizza party during
the final week of term and will
receive a raffle ticket for the chance
to win a

£50 Amazon voucher.

At Warboys Primary Academy, we
know that good attendance plays a
vital role in children's academic
achievement, social development and
wellbeing. Thank you for your
continued support in helping your
child attend school regularly and
arrive on time, giving them the very
best opportunity to thrive.

Term-time leave

We appreciate that unexpected events
can happen, and we’re always here to
support families where possible.

However, Cambridgeshire County
Council and the Department for
Education require schools to
authorise leave

only in exceptional
circumstances

—meaning rare,
unavoidable events.

Routine family holidays or planned
trips unfortunately do not meet this
threshold. You can find further
information here:

Non-attendance at school and the
law | Cambridgeshire County
Council

Thank you for your understanding
and cooperation.

We are incredibly proud to be able to

💛 Could you help keep our PTFA
going?

Our PTFA is a wonderful part of the
Warboys Primary Academy
community, helping to bring exciting
events and opportunities to our
children while raising much-needed
funds for the school.However,

we
urgently need more parents and carers
to get involved.

Following several of our valued
committee members stepping down
as their children finished at the
school last year, we are now facing a
very real challenge.

We are losing our
Treasurer, along with other
experienced members, and without
enough people willing to step forward,
we may have no choice but to fold the
PTFA.

We really don't want that to happen.
You might think you need lots of free
time or previous experience to join
the PTFA,

We need people
who can help in whatever way they
can. That could mean helping at an
event, coming along with ideas,
taking on a committee role, helping
with fundraising, or simply lending a
hand occasionally.

Every person who gets involved
makes the workload lighter for
everyone else — and helps us
continue providing those extra
experiences and opportunities
for our children.

Please come along, even if you're
unsure how you could help. Come and
meet the current PTFA, find out what
we do and see how you might be able
to get involved.

We genuinely need
your support. Without new volunteers,
the PTFA may not be able to continue.

Let's make sure we can keep doing
something really special for the
children of Warboys Primary
Academy.

high‑quality

through their Facebook page. It’s a
great way to save money, support the
school, and give uniform items a new
life.Please check out their page if you
need any extra bits for the term

If you require any further
information or have any questions or
concerns, please don’t hesitate to get
in touch with us in the school office -
we’re here to help.

Want to learn more? Take a look
around our website at

— you’ll find
plenty of helpful information.

REMEMBER - If you feel that a child
is unsafe, then please use the
following ways to contact help.

Call Social Services on 0345 045 5203
and make a referral. This can be an
anonymous referral if this feels safer.

Call 999 IF CHILD IS IN
IMMEDIATE DANGER.

You can also use our emergency email
address
(safeguarding@wpa.education). BUT
please use the other options first, so
as not to delay help for a child.

commemorations

announcements.title: Attendance Update: Termly Pizza Parties (TAPP) & Appointment Guidelines
announcements.content:
Attendance Update

As we begin the new academic year,
we are introducing a few updates to
our attendance procedures to support
pupils' success and celebrate excellent
attendance.

Medical appointments

will continue
to be authorised only when
appointment confirmation is provided
to the school office.

Optician
appointments

will no longer be
authorised from September, as these
can usually be arranged outside
school hours.

We are also delighted to launch our

Termly Attendance Pizza Parties
(TAPP).

Pupils achieving

98%
attendance or above

each term will be
invited to a special pizza party during
the final week of term and will
receive a raffle ticket for the chance
to win a

£50 Amazon voucher.

At Warboys Primary Academy, we
know that good attendance plays a
vital role in children's academic
achievement, social development and
wellbeing. Thank you for your
continued support in helping your
child attend school regularly and
arrive on time, giving them the very
best opportunity to thrive.

Term-time leave

We appreciate that unexpected events
can happen, and we’re always here to
support families where possible.

However, Cambridgeshire County
Council and the Department for
Education require schools to
authorise leave

only in exceptional
circumstances

—meaning rare,
unavoidable events.

Routine family holidays or planned
trips unfortunately do not meet this
threshold. You can find further
information here:

Non-attendance at school and the
law | Cambridgeshire County
Council

Thank you for your understanding

Cambridgeshire water leaks fill 86 Olympic pools every day, Lib Dems claim
metadata.contentSnippet: Cambridgeshire Liberal Democrat MPs have criticised Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch after analysis claimed trillions of litres of water had been lost to leaks across the East of England since the early 1990s.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Cambridgeshire water leaks fill 86 Olympic pools every day, Lib Dems claim
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Cambridgeshire Liberal Democrat MPs have attacked Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch after analysis claimed trillions of litres of water had been lost to leaks across the East of England since the early 1990s. The criticism comes after Kemi Badenoch reportedly described water privatisation as a “success”, a claim local Liberal Democrats have labelled “complete nonsense”. Liberal Democrat analysis of Ofwat data claims leaks from Anglian Water and Cambridge Water have wasted enough water to fill 86 Olympic-sized pools every day since records began in 1992. Ian Sollom MP says residents are being left 'high and dry' by water companies. (Image: Ian Sollom) The comments came jointly from Ian Sollom, MP for St Neots and Mid Cambridgeshire, Pippa Heylings, MP for South Cambridgeshire, Charlotte Cane, MP for Ely and East Cambridgeshire, and Cambridge prospective parliamentary candidate Cheney Payne. The politicians said the figures exposed decades of underinvestment in water infrastructure as Cambridgeshire residents faced supply cuts, low pressure and shortages at home. The group said they had heard from elderly and vulnerable residents affected by supply problems and claimed some had been left without adequate support or access to emergency water supplies. Charlotte Cane is the MP for Ely and East Cambridgeshire. (Image: Charlotte Cane) Mr Sollom said he had recently met representatives from Cambridge Water to discuss ongoing supply issues across the county. He said: “Residents have been left literally high and dry as the water supply keeps being cut off altogether or the pressure is so low, they can’t get more than a trickle out of their taps.” Mr Sollom said he urged the company to improve customer communications and register vulnerable residents for priority support during emergencies. The Liberal Democrats said water security was becoming more urgent in Cambridgeshire, one of the driest parts of the UK, as housing growth is expected to accelerate over the coming decades. The politicians said in a joint statement that the exceptionally hot, dry summer may have caused more burst pipes, but leaks had wasted water for decades. They also questioned whether existing infrastructure could cope with population growth and planned new homes. The party wants water companies turned into mutually owned public benefit corporations, with profits reinvested in infrastructure instead of paid to shareholders as dividends. The Conservatives have not responded to the Liberal Democrats’ comments. The Government has previously recognised Cambridgeshire's water supply crisis while setting out plans for regional growth. An Anglian Water spokesperson said: "Leakage remains one of our biggest priorities and we know customers expect us to keep reducing it. "Leakage levels on our network are around 40% lower than they were at privatisation, following sustained investment in finding and fixing leaks. Between 2025 and 2030, we're investing £348 million to renew more than 1,100km of water mains across our region."

metadata.title: Man bailed after protest camp outside puppy breeding facility cordoned off
metadata.contentSnippet: A man has been released on bail after Camp Beagle, outside MBR Acres in Wyton, Huntingdon, was cordoned off.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Man bailed after protest camp outside puppy breeding facility cordoned off
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A man has been released on bail after a protest camp outside a puppy breeding facility in Cambridgeshire was cordoned off. Police established a cordon around Camp Beagle, the UK's longest-running permanent animal rights protest camp, on Tuesday (October 6). The protest group has maintained a continuous presence outside MBR Acres in Wyton, Huntingdon, since the summer of 2021. Cambridgeshire Constabulary confirmed officers were at the scene as part of investigations into an alleged burglary at the controversial facility. The force was called to the facility on September 29 after reports that "a number of dogs" were allegedly taken from the site. A 43-year-old woman from Inverness was arrested on suspicion of burglary, with the incident believed to be linked to an "open rescue" at the site. A 63-year-old man, from Coventry, was later arrested on suspicion of conspiracy to burgle and was bailed until January 4, 2027. Have you got a story you want to share? Get in touch at oliver.murphy@newsquest.co.uk

metadata.title: Man bailed after boy seriously injured in three-vehicle crash
metadata.contentSnippet: A man arrested after a boy was seriously injured in a three-vehicle crash involving a pedestrian on the A1 near Peterborough has been bailed.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Man bailed after boy seriously injured in three-vehicle crash
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A man arrested after a boy was seriously injured in a three-vehicle crash involving a pedestrian on the A1 has been bailed. Police and paramedics were called at around 6.30pm on September 17 to the southbound carriageway at Thornaugh, near Peterborough. A white DAF lorry was involved in the collision with a stationary black Toyota Yaris. A 16-year-old boy from Peterborough who had got out of the Yaris suffered serious injuries and was rushed to Peterborough City Hospital. The HGV driver, a 54-year-old man from Wigan, was arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury by careless driving. In an update on Thursday (October 8), a spokesperson for Cambridgeshire Constabulary confirmed the man has been bailed until December 13. Police continue to appeal for witnesses and dashcam footage after the incident. Those who saw what happened or has footage should report it online, quoting reference 35/72248/26. metadata.title: Two men arrested inside RAF Molesworth released on bail
metadata.contentSnippet: Two men arrested inside RAF Molesworth in Cambridgeshire have been released on bail while police investigate.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Two men arrested inside RAF Molesworth released on bail
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Two men arrested inside an RAF base in Cambridgeshire have been released on bail while police investigate. The men, aged 32 and 36, were arrested at RAF Molesworth in the early hours of Thursday October 8 after being found inside the base perimeter. Both are Latvian nationals who live in the UK. They were taken to a Cambridgeshire police station before being released on bail with strict conditions. Counter Terrorism Policing London is leading the investigation, working with the Ministry of Defence Police (MDP) and Cambridgeshire Constabulary. At about 10pm on Wednesday, October 7, MDP security patrols near RAF Molesworth found an abandoned vehicle. Cambridgeshire officers joined them and the forces searched the site. Officers then found a small breach in the perimeter fence. Officers later found and arrested the men on suspicion of trespass and criminal damage. They were later arrested on suspicion of an offence under Section 4 of the National Security Act. This concerns entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the UK. Police have searched two addresses in the Peterborough area as part of the investigation. Officers also recovered the abandoned vehicle found near the base. Commander Helen Flanagan, Head of Counter Terrorism Policing London, said: “We’re very aware of the recent heightened interest and concern around military sites, but there is nothing from our investigation so far to suggest this incident is connected to the events at RAF Fairford last week.” She said: “A key line of enquiry remains to identify any potential motivation behind why the men were at that location, and this includes whether it may be connected to any criminal activity.” Police urged anyone who sees something that does not look or feel right to report it in confidence by calling 0800 789321. Reports can also be made online at www.gov.uk/ACT. The investigation continues in Cambridgeshire. Specialist explosive ordnance disposal officers carried out additional checks on the vehicle as a precaution, but found nothing of concern; a cordon affecting local roads, including part of the A1(M), was later lifted.

metadata.title: Seven road repair methods trialled on Cambridgeshire's peat roads in UK first
metadata.contentSnippet: Seven solutions to how to repair and maintain Cambridgeshire's peat soil-affected roads are currently being trialled along a Fenland highway.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Seven road repair methods trialled on Cambridgeshire's peat roads in UK first
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Seven solutions to how to repair and maintain Cambridgeshire's peat soil-affected roads are currently being trialled along a Fenland highway. The media were invited on Thursday to see how the trials aim to deliver longer-lasting repairs and better value for taxpayers’ money. Cllr Alex Beckett, chair of Cambridgeshire's highways and transport committee, Paul Bristow, the mayor of Cambridgeshire and Peterborough, joined representatives from the county council's project team and its project contractor, WinVic, to outline the work so far. Funded by the Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Combined Authority, the UK’s first trial of its kind is testing seven road-building techniques side by side to find the best solution for roads built on peat. Cllr Beckett highlighted the significant challenges peat soil roads, like the trial site in Upwell Road, March, cause highways authorities, pointing out that Cambridgeshire has around 1,000 miles of roads affected by peat. Fenland is home to 93 per cent of those roads, which is why the county council has selected the road in March. Seven 150-metre sections of road have been dug up, each for a different proposed solution. One section uses the current repair method as the control: plastic geogrid mesh is laid on the road surface, covered with road plainings and resurfaced with asphalt. Andy Harmon, framework manager for WinVic, the contractor working with Cambridgeshire County Council on the peat soil affected roads trial project. (Image: Sarah Cliss) The other construction methods being trialled are: This plastic mesh, known as Geogrid, is currently used in road repairs across Cambridgeshire and the country. (Image: Sarah Cliss) The trial will help identify which of the methods offers the best solution. Monitoring of Upwell Road will be carried out over three years using a variety of techniques, from gauges buried beneath the road surface to satellites taking detailed images to show any movement of the road surface, including sinking. Cllr Beckett said repairing a peat-affected road can cost up to five times more than repairing one built on other soil. Cambridgeshire Mayor Paul Bristow left on site in Upwell Road, March. (Image: Sarah Cliss) Not only that, but repairs last half as long as those carried out in other parts of the county. Cambridgeshire County Council receives no extra funding for the higher cost of repairing and maintaining its peat roads. Joshua Rutherford, the council’s head of asset management, design and delivery, said it needs £58.3m to maintain the status quo, but the Government provides £31.3m, leaving a £27m shortfall. James Chapman (left), project manager, with Joe McGilley, design engineer, holding a diagram showing the structure of one of the trials. (Image: Sarah Cliss) More money has been promised to tackle the repair backlog, but it will arrive over four years, with most coming at the end, leaving the council to find the cash upfront. It is hoped the trials will provide a better solution to the peat soil-affected roads, but which of the six options will prove the best is up for discussion, with those working on the site pinning their hopes on different methods. However, there was consensus on just how important the trials are to future maintenance of the county's roads, and satisfying residents fed up with negotiating undulating, pothole-riddled roads around Fenland. Cllr Alex Beckett, chair of Cambridgeshire's transport and highways committee, pointed out that a pint of peat soil contains the same amount of solids as a pint of milk. (Image: Sarah Cliss) This plastic mesh, known as Geogrid, is currently used in road repairs across Cambridgeshire and the country. (Image: Sarah Cliss) The council says peat-affected roads are contributing to an £800m backlog in road repairs across the county.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Cambridgeshire business leader appointed Deputy Lieutenant in recognition of service
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A business leader has been appointed as a Deputy Lieutenant of Cambridgeshire in recognition of her service to the community. Faye Holland, chair of the Cambridgeshire Chamber of Commerce board, will now support the Lord-Lieutenant of Cambridgeshire, Julie Spence, who serves as His Majesty The King’s representative in the county. Deputy Lieutenants are selected from across Cambridgeshire and may represent the Lord-Lieutenant at civic and ceremonial events, community occasions and Royal visits. Faye said: "I am deeply honoured to have been appointed as a Deputy Lieutenant of Cambridgeshire. "Cambridgeshire is an extraordinary county, defined by its people, communities, businesses and remarkable spirit of innovation. "I am incredibly proud to have the opportunity to serve the county in this new capacity and to support the Lord-Lieutenant in representing His Majesty The King across Cambridgeshire." She is also director of The Cambridge x Manchester Partnership and founder of the #21toWatch Technology Innovation Awards. Her career spans technology, communications, entrepreneurship and economic development, and she has held a range of mentoring, advisory and leadership roles supporting entrepreneurs and growing businesses. Charlotte Horobin, chief executive of Cambridgeshire Chamber of Commerce, said: "We are absolutely delighted for Faye. "This is a tremendous honour and a fitting recognition of the energy, commitment and leadership she has brought to Cambridgeshire over many years. "Faye has an exceptional ability to bring people together across business, academia, innovation and civic life, and she is a passionate champion for the county and its communities. "On behalf of everyone at the Chamber, our members and the Board, I would like to congratulate Faye on this very special appointment. "We are immensely proud to see our Chair take on this important role." Faye will continue as chair of the chamber board alongside her other professional commitments.

metadata.title: Police latest after pupil 'assaulted' at Cambridgeshire school
metadata.contentSnippet: An investigation launched after a student was "assaulted" at Cromwell Community College in Chatteris remains ongoing after more than two weeks.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Police latest after pupil 'assaulted' at Cambridgeshire school
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: An investigation launched after a pupil was "assaulted" at a school in Cambridgeshire remains ongoing after more than two weeks. Police received a report of an assault at Cromwell Community College, in Chatteris, on Wednesday (September 23). The incident is said to have taken place earlier in the day, Cambridgeshire Constabulary confirmed. The victim, a 13-year-old boy, attended hospital for treatment to his injuries and a crime for grievous bodily harm was raised. In a statement, the Active Learning Trust, which runs the school, revealed a Year 9 student was "hurt in an incident" . A spokesperson said staff "responded quickly and appropriately" and gave "care and support to the injured student". They added: "The college’s pastoral team has been supporting students following the incident and will continue to offer reassurance as required. "We will co-operate fully with the police and their investigation into this matter." In an update on Thursday (October 8), Cambridgeshire Constabulary confirmed the incident remains under investigation. Have you got a story you want to share? metadata.title: Swimming pool plans for industrial unit refused over parking and safety concerns
metadata.contentSnippet: Huntingdonshire District Council has rejected plans to turn an industrial unit in St Ives into a community swimming pool, despite backing from education, health and swimming groups.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Swimming pool plans for industrial unit refused over parking and safety concerns
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Find, save and share Public Notices that affect you in the  area. The Public Notice Portal carries statutory public notices published in local newspapers and is the fastest and most effective way of finding out what is happening in YOUR neighbourhood. Huntingdonshire District Council has rejected plans to turn an industrial unit in St Ives into a community swimming pool, despite backing from education, health and swimming groups. Spencer Smith applied to convert 1 Bramley Road from a motorcycle repair workshop into an indoor pool offering swimming lessons, water safety training, hydrotherapy, aqua fitness and rehabilitation. Council planners acknowledged the community benefits of the proposal but concluded that insufficient information had been provided to address concerns over parking, public safety, noise and site selection. In its decision notice, the council said it had not been demonstrated that the development could operate within the established employment area without causing amenity and public safety issues because of a lack of parking provision. Officers also said the application did not properly explain why other sites had been ruled out. A second reason for refusal related to a lack of information about the proposed air conditioning unit and plant equipment. Environmental Health officers said there was insufficient detail to assess whether noise could affect nearby homes. The third refusal reason was parking: the four proposed spaces, including one accessible bay, were not enough for staff and users and could cause overspill on nearby industrial-estate roads. St Ives Town Council objected over highway and pedestrian safety, parking, the site layout and public safety. But the report said Cambridgeshire County Council’s highways team raised no highway-safety objection. Four organisations submitted letters supporting the scheme. One of the strongest endorsements came from the Swimming Teachers' Association, which said there was an ongoing shortage of suitable facilities for lessons and training. It argued the pool would provide opportunities for swimming education, professional qualifications, fitness activities and accessible sessions for people with additional needs. Wyton-on-the-Hill Primary School also backed the proposal, saying similar small teaching pools were often better suited to helping children gain confidence in the water than larger leisure-centre facilities. The school said it would be likely to use a purpose-built St Ives teaching pool because it would cut travel times. A local physiotherapy practice said the pool could offer swimming lessons, water aerobics and hydrotherapy, while specialist hydrotherapy was limited locally. A Cambridgeshire Pilates instructor also backed the plan, saying demand for aqua aerobics was high and classes at One Leisure St Ives were oversubscribed. The applicant’s planning statement said the pool would tackle a waiting list of more than 100 children, create jobs and bring a potentially vacant building back into use. It also said the pool could create at least eight direct jobs, plus work for independent instructors and specialist providers. But planning officers said the benefits did not outweigh concerns about parking, public safety, noise and the lack of evidence for choosing the site. Planning officers recommended refusal, and the council rejected the application. The applicant, Spencer Smith, also runs the local swim school Splash & Learn, where he teaches children to swim.

metadata.title: Huntingdon Town Council given go ahead to fly Pride and Pan-African flags
metadata.contentSnippet: Huntingdon Town Council has won permission to fly the Progress Pride and Pan-African flags from its historic Town Hall balcony, months after it was criticised for displaying them without consent.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Huntingdon Town Council given go ahead to fly Pride and Pan-African flags
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Find, save and share Public Notices that affect you in the  area. The Public Notice Portal carries statutory public notices published in local newspapers and is the fastest and most effective way of finding out what is happening in YOUR neighbourhood. Huntingdon Town Council has won permission to fly the Progress Pride and Pan-African flags from its historic Town Hall balcony, months after it was criticised for displaying them without consent. The issue surfaced earlier this year when it emerged that the Grade II* listed Town Hall in Market Hill had been flying flags without the planning consent required under advertising rules. Huntingdonshire District Council has now granted consent for the two flags to be flown each year from the building’s existing balcony flagpoles. Huntingdon Town Council applied to fly the Progress Pride flag throughout Pride Month in June and the Pan-African flag during Black History Month in October. Planning documents accompanying the application acknowledged that both flags fell into a category requiring express consent before they could be displayed on the Town Hall. The council’s new Flag Flying Policy says the Progress Pride and Pan-African flags are "subject to planning consent". In supporting documents, the council said the flags were intended to celebrate nationally recognised cultural and community events and reflect the town's diversity, inclusivity and community values. Officials stressed they would only be displayed during designated commemorative periods and would not be permanent fixtures. A planning officer’s report said the flags would not harm the historic Town Hall, the Huntingdon Conservation Area or public safety. The report said the flags would use existing poles without adding visual clutter, while Cambridgeshire County Council’s highways authority raised no objection. No public representations were received during the consultation period. The approval covers the Progress Pride and Pan-African flags on the Town Hall’s projecting balcony flagpoles from October 2026 to October 2031. The decision gives the council formal approval to fly the flags after it came under scrutiny for displaying them without consent, as previously reported by the Hunts Post. The council’s Flag Flying Policy allows other flags, including the Union Flag, St George’s Cross and Huntingdonshire flag, to fly at scheduled civic and commemorative events. But flags without automatic consent must first be approved by the local planning authority. The council has previously clarified that, unlike the traditional Gilbert Baker Pride flag, the Progress Pride flag does not benefit from deemed consent under advertising regulations and therefore needs express approval.

metadata.title: Convicted paedophile found with indecent images sent back to prison
metadata.contentSnippet: A convicted paedophile from Huntingdon is back behind bars after accessing indecent images of children, breaching the conditions of a court order.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Convicted paedophile found with indecent images sent back to prison
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A convicted paedophile from Cambridgeshire is back behind bars after being found with indecent images of children, breaching the conditions of a court order. John Ashcroft, 32, was given a sexual harm prevention order until 2032, following a previous conviction for making indecent images of children. As part of the conditions of his order police installed monitoring software on his devices to alert them if he tried to access illegal material. On March 15, 2025, the software on Ashcroft’s device alerted officers to suspicious activity on his account. Police seized Ashcroft’s computer and mobile phone for forensic examination and discovered indecent images of children on both. Ashcroft, of Judson Court, Huntingdon, pleaded guilty to breaching his sex offender requirements and three counts of making indecent images of children. He was sentenced to one year and one month in prison at Peterborough Crown Court on Thursday October 1. Detective Constable Kerry Howard, from the force’s management of sexual offenders and violent offenders team (MOSOVO), said: "Officers from MOSOVO will always check on convicted sex offenders in the county to make sure they are adhering to their conditions and court orders. "In this case, pre-installed software helped us uncover further offences and bring Ashcroft to justice.” Have you got a story you want to share? metadata.title: Rudimental to headline huge outdoor concert at Thetford Forest
metadata.contentSnippet: Drum and bass giants Rudimental are set to perform a huge outdoor concert at Thetford Forest.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Rudimental to headline huge outdoor concert at Thetford Forest
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Drum and bass giants Rudimental are set to perform a huge outdoor concert near Cambridgeshire. The chart-topping group will headline a concert at High Lodge, in Thetford Forest, as part of Forestry England’s Forest Live 2027 concert series. Rudimental will take to the stage on Wednesday June 16, with special guests Girls Don’t Sync and MJ Cole. A spokesperson for Forestry England said: "Rudimental are a genre-bending British electronic group formed in Hackney, east London, in 2010. "They previously played Forest Live shows at Thetford Forest in 2016. "Known for their energetic live performances, the trio blend drum and bass, jungle, soul, grime, and electronica, and have released multiple chart-topping albums." The group, made up of Piers Aggett, Kesi Dryden, and Leon "Locksmith" Rolle, first shot to fame with their 2012 hit Feel the Love. Since then, they have sold more than 25 million singles and three million albums worldwide, earning three UK No.1 singles and two UK No.1 albums. Their latest album, Rudimental, includes the top 10 single Dancing Is Healing and collaborations with stars such as Popcaan, Idris Elba, and Khalid. A spokesperson said: "Forestry England manages and cares for the nation’s 1,500 woods and forests, planting more than seven million trees each year. "Funds raised from Forest Live events help support conservation projects and the ongoing maintenance of these natural spaces." The Forest Live concert series marks its 25th anniversary in 2026. Over the past 25 years, more than 2.5 million people have attended the events. Tickets for Rudimental’s 2027 Forest Live shows go on general sale at 10am on Friday, October 16, via forestlive.com. Fans can sign up on the website for updates, announcements, and exclusive pre-sale access.

metadata.title: Navy sailor accused of plotting to leak intelligence to Russia appears in court
metadata.contentSnippet: A Royal Navy sailor accused of plotting to leak classified information to Russia has appeared in court.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Navy sailor accused of plotting to leak intelligence to Russia appears in court
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Royal Navy sailor accused of plotting to leak classified information to Russia has appeared in court for the first time. Teddy Young, 24, is alleged to have abused his high-level security clearance to access secret defence and intelligence data after being deployed on a Navy vessel. It is said he had drafted a message in Russian containing classified information and had allegedly taken steps to make direct contact with the Russian authorities. Young, who lives in a semi-detached house in the village of Clapham, on the outskirts of Bedford, appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Thursday to face the charges for the first time. "The allegation is that while serving as a Royal Navy warfare intelligence rating with high-level security clearance and intelligence-system access, Teddy Stanley Greenidge Young accessed and retained sensitive UK defence and intelligence material and engaged in activity consistent with preparing to pass protected information to a foreign power," the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) told the court in a written summary of the allegations. It is said Young, who joined the Navy in April 2024, committed the offences on his first deployment, which began on November 4, 2024. He is accused of using the dark web to try to make contact with Russian authorities, drafting a message which "sought to make contact with a potential threat actor", and breaking Navy rules by copying information to a private email account. Young wore a grey sweatshirt and joggers as he appeared in the dock in front of District Judge Annabel Pilling. He was arrested by counter-terror police at his home in Bedfordshire on Tuesday, having previously been arrested in Hampshire last year. He is charged with engaging in conduct preparatory to the commission of an offence under the National Security Act 2023 and a second allegation of obtaining, accepting or retaining material benefit from a designated body. According to the charges, it is said that between November 26, 2024 and May 21, 2025 Young "disclosed protected information for a purpose which he knew, or having regard to other matters known to him ought reasonably to have known, was prejudicial to the safety or interests of the UK intending the conduct to benefit a foreign power, engaged in conduct in preparation for the commission of such an act". Over the same six-month period, Young is said to have "obtained, copied, recorded or retained protected information, intending the conduct to benefit a foreign power". Young was not asked to enter any pleas during the four-minute court hearing on Thursday. The judge told him: "As you know the matters that you have been charged with are too serious to be dealt with at this court and need to be dealt with at a crown court." Judge Pilling sent the case to the Old Bailey, where Young is due to appear on October 16, and remanded him in custody. When announcing the charge, police stressed there was no link between this investigation and the ongoing RAF Fairford probe. A Royal Navy spokesman said: "A member of the Royal Navy has been charged with National Security Act offences following an investigation by Counter Terrorism Policing London. "As legal proceedings are ongoing, it would be inappropriate to comment further at this stage."

metadata.title: 'Calculated' man accepted neighbour's parcel before plotting burglary
metadata.contentSnippet: A man from Hemingford Grey who had been trusted to accept a delivery for his neighbour plotted a burglary when he realised their house was empty.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: 'Calculated' man accepted neighbour's parcel before plotting burglary
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A man who had been trusted to accept a delivery for his neighbour plotted a burglary when he realised their house was empty. Sam Biddle, 51, of Margetts, Hemingford Grey, accepted the delivery while his neighbour was away from home. After realising the property was unoccupied, he used that knowledge to plan a break-in. At 6.22pm, he left the parcel by the front door of the house. Later that evening, between 8.08pm and 9.35pm, Biddle returned to the address several times wearing gloves and a face covering. During the attempted burglary, he tried the front door and removed a CCTV camera. He also attempted to force open a side door and smashed a windowpane in an effort to gain entry. Police were called after the victim received notifications from the CCTV camera to his phone. Biddle was identified by detectives from the CCTV and arrested. At Peterborough Crown Court on October 1, Biddle was sentenced to two years and three months in prison. He admitted attempted burglary and activating a previous suspended sentence. Detective Sergeant Jonathan Lockwood said: "This was a calculated offence committed by someone who took advantage of a position of trust. "Having accepted a parcel on behalf of his neighbour, Biddle realised the property was empty and saw it as an opportunity to commit a burglary. "He returned repeatedly, concealing his identity and making determined efforts to get inside. "Thankfully, the home’s security system alerted the victim to what was happening, allowing offices to respond, leading to Biddle’s arrest." Have you got a story you want to share? Get in touch at oliver.murphy@newsquest.co.uk or newsdesk@huntspost.co.uk

metadata.title: Counter-terror police investigating after two men arrested at Cambs RAF base
metadata.contentSnippet: Counter terror police have launched an investigation after two men were arrested on suspicion of trespass offences at the RAF Molesworth base in Cambridgeshire.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Counter-terror police investigating after two men arrested at Cambs RAF base
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Counter terror police have launched an investigation after two men were arrested on suspicion of trespass offences at an RAF base in Cambridgeshire. Security patrols by Ministry of Defence Police at RAF Molesworth identified an abandoned vehicle at 10pm on Wednesday (October 7). Officers from Cambridgeshire Constabulary also attended and carried out further searches of the area where a small breach in the perimeter fence was identified. At 2am the next day, two men, aged 36 and 32, were arrested inside the base perimeter. They were initially arrested on suspicion of trespass on a prohibited site and criminal damage and taken to a police station. The pair have since been further arrested on suspicion of an offence under section 4 of the National Security Act 2023. Both men remain in police custody at this time. Officers are carrying out two searches at addresses in the Peterborough area in connection with the investigation. The abandoned vehicle was recovered by police and taken to a nearby location. While undergoing further searches, concerns over the vehicle led to the deployment of specialist ‘EOD’ officers to carry out additional checks. As a precaution, a cordon was in place, which impacted on local roads in the Glatton area, including part of the A1(M). However, after assessment by specialist officers, nothing of concern was found and all cordons have since been lifted. The incident is now being investigated by officers from Counter Terrorism Policing. Commander Helen Flanagan, Head of Counter Terrorism Policing London, said: “We’re very aware of the recent heightened interest and concern around military sites, but at this stage there is nothing to suggest this incident is connected to the events at RAF Fairford last week. "Our investigation into this incident is at its very early stages. A big part of this is looking at any potential motivation as to why the men were present at the site, but I must stress we are keeping an open mind at this stage and enquiries are very much ongoing. "As ever, I would ask the public to remain vigilant and if you see anything of concern, then to contact police." Have you got a story you want to share? Get in touch at oliver.murphy@newsquest.co.uk

metadata.title: Prolific thief targeted shops and businesses including bakery
metadata.contentSnippet: A prolific thief who targeted shops and businesses, including Tesco and Co-op, across Cambridge has been jailed.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Prolific thief targeted shops and businesses including bakery
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A prolific thief who targeted shops and businesses across Cambridge has been jailed. Jack Wilmot, of no fixed address, admitted a series of burglaries, thefts and assaults against shop workers over a two-week period. Between August 21 and September 4, he carried out repeated offences at shops where he climbed over the till area to take cigarettes and alcohol. On two occasions he assaulted members of staff. Wilmot also broke into Dorringtons Bakery and stole a charity box as well as breaking into Milton Road Pharmacy. The 29-year-old stole perfume, alcohol and meat worth almost £600 from Tesco, John Lewis, Co-op and Sainsbury’s. At Cambridge Magistrates’ Court on Friday (October 2), Wilmot was sentenced to a year in prison. He pleaded guilty to nine counts of burglary, two counts of common assault and four counts of theft. He was also handed a five-year Criminal Behaviour Order. This bans him from any Marks and Spencer, John Lewis, Co-op, Sainsbury’s or Tesco shop within the boundary of the A14, M11 and A11. Wilmot must pay a total of £2,469 in compensation to retailers Co-op, John Lewis, Sainsbury’s, Tesco as well as the victims he assaulted. Detective Constable Zoe Bramley, said: "Wilmot’s offending had a significant impact on retailers and their staff, who were repeatedly targeted over a short period of time. "His crime escalated from shop thefts to burglaries and assaults on shop workers carrying out their jobs. "This sentence, along with the Criminal Behaviour Order, demonstrates that persistent offending will not be tolerated and that we will continue to work with businesses to protect staff and bring people like Wilmot to justice" Have you got a story you want to share? Serving Royal Navy member charged with spying after Bedfordshire arrest
metadata.contentSnippet: A serving member of the Royal Navy has been charged with spying following an arrest in Bedfordshire.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Serving Royal Navy member charged with spying after Bedfordshire arrest
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A serving member of the Royal Navy has been charged with spying following his arrest in Bedfordshire. Teddy Young, 24, will appear in court on today (October 8) accused of obtaining protected information which could benefit a unnamed foreign power, the Metropolitan Police said. Young was arrested by counter-terror police at his home in Bedfordshire on Tuesday, having previously been arrested in Hampshire last year. He will appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court facing charges that between November 2024 and May 2025 he "engaged in conduct in preparation for committing an offence of disclosing protected information, contrary to section 18 of the National Security Act 2023". Between the same dates it is also alleged he "obtained, copied, recorded or retained protected information, intending the conduct to benefit a foreign power, knowing or having regard to other matters known to him ought reasonably to know was prejudicial to the safety or interests of the United Kingdom, contrary to section 1 of the National Security Act 2023". Police stressed there was no link between this investigation and the ongoing RAF Fairford probe. Commander Helen Flanagan, Head of Counter Terrorism Policing London, said: "These are very serious charges against a serving member of the armed forces. We have worked extremely closely with relevant operational colleagues within the Ministry of Defence as our investigation has progressed to ensure appropriate measures could be taken to mitigate any potential risks linked to this matter." A Royal Navy spokesman said: "A member of the Royal Navy has been charged with National Security Act (NSA) offences following an investigation by Counter Terrorism Policing London. As legal proceedings are ongoing, it would be inappropriate to comment further at this stage."

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A "violent" arsonist from Cambridgeshire who smashed up his ex-partner's home and chased her with a hammer has been jailed. Anthony Lamb, 51, showed up at his partner’s home in Histon, near Cambridge, on July 30 and began causing damage before trying to attack her with a hammer. The victim managed to escape to a nearby property and call police. When officers arrived, they discovered a fire had been started close to the victim’s front door. They managed to extinguish it and promptly arrested Lamb. Lamb, of Church Street, Gamlingay, pleaded guilty to two counts of criminal damage and breach of a restraining order. He was sentenced to a total of three years and six months in prison at Peterborough Crown Court on Thursday October 1. Detective Constable Jack Sillince, who investigated, said: "Lamb launched a violent and frightening attack against his ex-partner. "If she hadn’t escaped to her neighbour’s and if the fire had taken hold this could have been even worse. “I am glad justice has been done and hope Lamb reflects on his actions while behind bars." Plans have been submitted to install a permanent hot-food takeaway trailer in a Huntingdonshire village. Poopalasingam Thillaivarothayan is seeking permission to change the use of land at a property in Fenstanton for the food trailer. Application documents, submitted on September 25, say the trailer would be installed permanently on the applicant’s premises. The floor plan shows a trailer measuring about 4.5 metres by 2.4 metres, with fryers, hot plates, refrigeration units and preparation areas. The site would include outdoor storage for general waste, mixed recycling and food waste. The documents state that the containers would be kept closed to prevent odours and vermin and the storage area would be cleaned regularly. The application says contamination risks would be minimal because the food team would manage operational waste. It also says flood risk at the site is low. Noise would be reduced by servicing exhaust fans, using insulated or quieter commercial appliances and restricting operating hours. The measures are intended to limit disturbance to neighbouring properties. metadata.title: Further arrest as police continue to investigate 'violent disorder' in town

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Police have made another arrest after violent disorder in a Huntingdonshire town which left two men with serious injuries. Officers received multiple calls to The Broadway, in St Ives, on the evening of August 29, reporting violence and criminal damage in the town centre. Two men were taken to hospital where they were treated for serious but not life threatening injuries. Last month, Cambridgeshire Constabulary revealed six people had been arrested in connection with the incident. Two 19-year-old men, from Hartford and St Ives, were arrested on suspicion of a public order offence. A 20-year-old man from Huntingdon was arrested on suspicion of a public order offence and possession of drugs. A 29-year-old woman from Wyton was also arrested on suspicion of a public order offence. Meanwhile, a 19-year-old man from Whittlesey was arrested on suspicion of assault occasioning grievous bodily harm. They have all been bailed pending further enquiries and further arrests are expected in the coming weeks, the force confirmed. A sixth person, a man from Chatteris, was arrested on suspicion of a public order offence but has since been released without charge. In an update on Tuesday (October 6), a spokesperson confirmed a 17-year-old boy from Saffron Walden, in Essex, was arrested on suspicion of affray. He has since been released on bail until October 26, 2027. Detective Inspector Luke Pedlar said: "Our investigation has progressed quickly and we have already made a number of arrests, with further enquiries ongoing. "We are committed to identifying everyone involved and ensuring they are held accountable for their actions. "I would like to thank the community for their support so far and continue to urge anyone with information, footage or who witnessed the disorder to come forward and speak to us." metadata.title: Awards will spotlight sustainable workplaces and energy champions
metadata.contentSnippet: Meet the judges for the Sustainable Workplace of the Year and East of England Energy Ambassador categories at the East Anglia Clean & Green Awards 2027.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Awards will spotlight sustainable workplaces and energy champions
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: With innovators operating across multiple sectors, the East of England is playing a significant role in advancing sustainable business across the UK. This is what the East Anglia Clean & Green Awards are all about, and the Sustainable Workplace of the Year and East of England Energy Ambassador awards will spotlight the progressive, sustainable local organisations and people who are contributing to the region’s growing reputation. Here, the judges for these categories tell us more about what they’ll be looking for in the winners. James Groves, managing director of Indigo Swan (Image: Indigo Swan) Sponsored by Indigo Swan James Groves, managing director, Indigo Swan Why were you keen to get involved in the Clean & Green Awards? As a respected energy consultant in Norfolk, I felt it was important that Indigo Swan supported these awards and helped to bring attention to the amazing businesses across the region that are really making a statement when it comes to sustainability and net zero. What do you bring to the judging process? I bring more than 16 years’ experience within the energy sector, an understanding of the sustainable market and an ISO14001 accreditation. Through my experience at Indigo Swan – beginning as commercial director in 2018, becoming MD in 2019 and leading a management buyout in 2022 – I also have a clear understanding of how behavioural and cultural change in a business can impact your journey to being more sustainable and how important it will be on the journey to net zero. Have you ever been judged for an award yourself. If so, how will you use that experience when judging this award? Yes. The key for me is making sure that the award, if it’s for a company, is written by the company. We want to convey what the business does, stands for and is implementing. I want to see clear examples of where change has taken place. Statistics that can be proven and the understanding of change within an organisation are areas to focus on. I’ll also be looking for evidence of the impact on the people within the business and, of course, passion – all areas that have helped us with our success. What will you be looking for in the winner? A great combination of investment, behavioural change and a clear understanding of how being sustainable has helped to grow the business financially and improved the culture and engagement of the staff. The winner will show what best practice looks like, supported through facts, figures and accreditations. What advice would you give to anyone that’s considering entering? Do it. What do you have to lose? You have to buy a ticket to win the raffle. It will show your business as a shining light for how being more sustainable should be managed, and it will create a number of new opportunities. Ian Pease, business development manager at GENERATE (Image: Departure Lounge Media Group) Sponsored by GENERATE Ian Pease, business development manager, GENERATE Can you tell us a bit about your career to date? I am responsible for business development at OrbisEnergy, a clean energy business hub in Lowestoft, Suffolk. I have 25 years’ experience in the energy sector, during which time I’ve worked in both the public and private sectors in economic development, skills and competence, oil and gas, offshore wind, project management and business development. Part of my job is to manage GENERATE, established by local authorities in Norfolk, Suffolk and Essex to attract and support inward investment and business growth in the East of England’s energy sector. Why were you keen to get involved in the Clean & Green Awards? I wanted to get involved in these awards because I think it’s important for business leaders to be associated with such a high-profile awards programme and support the East Anglia Clean & Green initiative. What do you bring to the judging process? I’ve been in the energy sector for many years and have seen lots of new technologies come to the market. I’ve also seen firsthand how the composition of the East of England’s energy sector is changing, as it continues on its journey to a fully decarbonisation energy system. What will you be looking for in the winner? As the award category name suggests, I’ll be looking for a genuine ambassador for the East of England’s energy sector. In my opinion, the winner will be someone who’s making a difference and driving our region’s energy sector in a positive direction. What advice would you give to anyone that’s considering entering? My advice for entrants is to take time with your application and make sure you include all the good work you’re doing and your plans for the future, too. The deadline for entries to the East Anglia Clean & Green Awards is November 8 at midnight. For more information or to enter, visit cleanandgreenawards.co.uk

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Cambridgeshire man has pleaded guilty to defrauding a woman out of a six-figure sum. Kambiz Akhondi appeared at Peterborough Crown Court on Tuesday (October 6) after being charged with fraud by abuse of position. The 60-year-old initially pleaded not guilty but changed this after the judge indicated he would not face more than three years in prison if he changed his plea. His defence had sought a Goodyear indication, which allows the judge to tell a defendant what the maximum sentence will be before they plead guilty. Akhondi, of Calfe Fen Close, Soham, was accused of transferring sums amounting to around £126k from Maud Miller’s bank account to his own. The offence happened between October 24, 2018, and March 17, 2020, while he was in a position of power over her finances. The court heard that Akhondi was expected to safeguard her estate and not act against her financial interests, but transferred the sums for his own gain. Akhondi was released on unconditional bail and is due to reappear in court to be sentenced on November 18.

metadata.title: 'Awesome' Roman cremation urn and ploughshare found at Cambridgeshire dig
metadata.contentSnippet: An 'awesome' cremation urn was the big find at an archaeological dig in Cambridgeshire, which was a new attempt to locate a Roman villa.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: 'Awesome' Roman cremation urn and ploughshare found at Cambridgeshire dig
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: An 'awesome' cremation urn was the big find at an archaeological dig in Cambridgeshire, which was a new attempt to locate a Roman villa. Run by DigVentures, the two-week excavation was crowdfunded, with some of those donating working alongside professional archaeologists to find out more about the site, located in the countryside close to Sacrewell, on the outskirts of Peterborough. In the 1970s, archaeologists found remains of a winged Roman villa, including furnaces, painted plaster and tiled floors, but never uncovered the villa itself. The ploughshare was found alongside the glass cremation urn.. (Image: Jacob Reader) Fifty years on Nat Jackson, site director, and his team from DigVentures set about unearthing more of the villa's story, and that of the people who lived there, and also to make a fresh attempt to locate it. In two weeks, they excavated three trenches and found pottery, coins, roof tiles, underfloor-heating tiles, snail and oyster shells and, most excitingly, the cremation burial. The excavators found a blue glass urn in the remains of a wooden box, alongside an iron ploughshare - the cutting or leading edge of a plough. Reporter Sarah Cliss joined the DigVentures team for the last day of the dig. (Image: Sarah Cliss) Nat believes it could have belonged to someone who lived in the villa and perhaps farmed the land. "It is possible the person thought, 'I am a farmer; I want to be buried with farming tools', that's so cool, and it's a really awesome thing to find. I have never found anything like it before," he said. It was Nat's job to draw up the specifics for the dig, researching as much as he could about the site and determining where the exploration trenches should go. Geophysical surveys have been carried out of the site to help locate the site of the Roman villa and the best place to dig exploration trenches. (Image: Jacob Reader) Geophysical surveys of the site also helped with that, and there were high hopes of finding a furnace in one of the trenches, which had shown a large iron deposit, but digging showed it was a false alarm when a large iron horseshoe was discovered. “It was massive, probably from a shire horse or something like that dating to the 18th century or 19th century, but it was not what we were hoping to find,” said Nat. Harriet Tatton, senior project officer for project development at DigVentures, was equally excited by the burial find. Volunteers worked alongside professional archaeologists at the site near Sacrewell. (Image: Jacob Reader) She said the urn's hexagonal shape had helped to date it to around the 2nd century AD - so 1,800 years ago, give or take 100 years - so around the Antonine period or possibly to the time of the Emperor Flavian. The urn’s contents will be excavated carefully off-site in the hope of revealing more about the person buried inside. It is easy to make assumptions that it was a man because the person was buried with a ploughshare, but it could be a female and if we are lucky, we might be able to discover which. Volunteers worked alongside professional archaeologists at the site near Sacrewell. (Image: Jacob Reader) Harriet said it was common for people to be buried with objects that meant something to the people in life, but it should be remembered that the choices would most likely have been made by their family, not by the person themselves. Some of the volunteers were sponsored to join the dig through the online adult learning App Nibble, which also allowed me to join the fun for the day. Like the many other volunteers working alongside the professionals, I was given a trowel, a brush and bucket and set to work cleaning the stones of earth in one of the excavation ditches. Volunteers worked alongside professional archaeologists at the site near Sacrewell. (Image: Jacob Reader) The aim was to reveal the natural geology of the area and to show the ditches that had been dug by the Roman occupiers of the site, ready for detailed work off-site. The other volunteers came from across the country; some had donated to the crowdfunding appeal, while others had received the dig as a gift. One man, who was a huge fan of Channel 4's Time Team hosted by Tony Robinson, had always dreamed of joining a dig and had been given the chance as a 60th birthday present from his wife. Volunteers and professionals worked side by side to unearth the secrets buried at the site near Sacrewell. (Image: Jacob Reader) Another had received it as a retirement gift. Both thoroughly enjoyed getting stuck in and were excited when they unearthed a piece of roof tile. One woman from Leicestershire was delighted that she had been given a chance to help unearth the urn. “I can't believe I got to work on something so precious. I told my family not to tell the team just how clumsy I can be, as I didn't want to miss out; it was so special,” she said. Volunteers worked alongside professional archaeologists at the site near Sacrewell. (Image: Jacob Reader) Another man from Kent said it had reawakened an old passion, and that it was wonderful to pull a piece of history out of the ground and hold it in his hand. Harriet said all the finds would be cleaned, examined and catalogued. The urn, ploughshare and coins could go to a museum, while less significant items may be reburied. metadata.title: School responds after inspection uncovers fire safety 'deficiencies'
metadata.contentSnippet: Longsands Academy in St Neots, which is run by the Astrea Academy Trust, has reassured parents after several "deficiencies" were unearthed during a recent fire safety inspection.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: School responds after inspection uncovers fire safety 'deficiencies'
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A school in Huntingdonshire has reassured parents after "deficiencies" were unearthed during a recent fire safety inspection. Cambridgeshire Fire and Rescue Service visited Longsands Academy, in St Neots, at the end of September, it has been revealed. In a letter seen by The Hunts Post, the inspection was organised to assess concerns raised about the safety of the premises. Fire safety officers unearthed several deficiencies under the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005. It comes after two sources approached this newspaper to raise concerns about fire safety at Longsands, which is run by the Astrea Academy Trust. The school has since confirmed it is working to resolve the issues, which include a defective fire alarm sounder and a damaged set of fire doors. Inspectors raised concerns about a set of fire safety doors in N Block (Image: Supplied) In a letter to parents, the school said the site is "considered to be safe and complies overwhelmingly" with required fire safety standards. It added: "The inspection highlighted one or two minor deficiencies which our site team is now working on to resolve. "The fire safety inspectors found that the fire alarm sounder in H Block is faulty, due to a defect on the fire panel, and that some emergency lighting is not working properly. "They also said that two fire-resisting doors in N Block needed to be repaired, after some damage was caused. "However, the inspectors are satisfied that we are working to put these issues right and do not feel the need to re-inspect the school." Longsands Academy revealed the fire doors had been damaged (Image: Supplied) It continues: "I would like to take this opportunity to remind parents and carers of the important role families play in supporting Longsands’ approach to appropriate student behaviour. "In recent weeks, some damage has been caused to school property by students and we would ask you to reinforce at home the expectations we have around respect and responsibility." A spokesperson for Cambridgeshire Fire and Rescue Service confirmed officers "arranged for a further visit at the end of September." They added: "A minor deficiencies notice was issued to the Responsible Person, which was focussed on routine maintenance issues. "The Responsible Person has been fully engaged in the process and proactive in addressing the highlighted deficiencies." Have you got a story you want to share? Camp Beagle, the UK's longest-running permanent animal rights protest camp, has maintained a continuous presence outside MBR Acres since the summer of 2021. Camp Beagle is stationed outside MBR Acres in Huntingdon (Image: Newsquest) The organisation demands that the facility close and end the use of beagles for research purposes.
